correctness.rationale: Checkerboard parity forces every admissible set to have at most six vertices. Independent exact enumeration, not execution of the frozen checker, reproduced 4811 and 27597 faces, 2363 and 13518 pairs, and complete acyclic orders of the 21992 and 130886 directed incidences. The critical cells are one vertex and 84 or 560 five-cells, so Forman's CW model has nothing in the target of the five-cell attaching maps except a point. The nonempty oriented alternating face traces, in the frozen order, are (-83,1,-3,1,11,11,11,11) and (-559,1,1,1,1,1,29,29); subtracting the augmentation and negating gives the asserted characters. Independent fixed-triple counts with determinant signs agree; ordinary rational characters determine the rational representations. Barycentric subdivision makes the group action without inversions, so rational quotient chains identify with coinvariants and averaging identifies these with invariants. The averages are 6 and 63. value.rationale: The finite square cases and actions are naturally motivated, but they are already known at full strength. The frozen result does not prove a general equivariant construction or a new invariant beyond translating the existing character by elementary permutation-cycle counting and averaging. A reproducible second certificate is useful as verification, not a separate finding at this scope.
